- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; adjust upward, particularly if recent price is trending down.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp upward moves (e.g., +5–10% in 1–2 days); apply a “cool-down” correction by reducing forecast by 1–3% for the next 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative (or vice versa) within 3–5 days, model often lags; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead of sentiment change.
- For 30-day forecasts, avoid extreme outliers (>±15% from 14-day moving average); cap or clip forecasts to prevent overconfidence in volatility.
